item.title: Rare-Earth Supply Chains: Refining Bottlenecks and Geopolitical Leverage
item.author: blog@baifan.site (ByF (BaiFan))
item.description:
Global defense and clean-energy supply chains rely on rare-earth elements not merely through raw deposit extraction, but through high-purity chemical separation, patent infrastructure, and chemical engineering scale.

China: The Global Manufacturing Power Holding the Rare Earths Initiative
#

Against a backdrop of international turbulence, China — on the strength of long-term industrial accumulation and technical capability — holds a firm dominant position in the rare earth metals and magnets market. These rare earth materials are the core inputs of missiles, fighter jets, drones, submarines and even the new-energy industries, earning them the name “vitamins of industry.”

item.title: Global Trends and Geopolitics: Reading The Economist, November 2025
item.author: blog@baifan.site (ByF (BaiFan))
item.description:
The November 2025 issue of The Economist sketches a fractured global architecture: an escalating tech war between Washington and Beijing on one side, and defensive contraction alongside balance-sheet recession risks across major economies on the other.

Politics and Diplomacy: Strategic Decoupling Without Departure
#

  • US-China rivalry in semiconductors and infrastructure continues to escalate: new export controls meet supply-chain rerouting and localized component substitution.
  • Beijing deepens bilateral ties across the Middle East and the Global South through energy and industrial infrastructure pacts.
  • Domestic governance doubles down on preserving baseline stability amidst external containment.

US-China “decoupling” is like a separation where nobody moves out: they shout about breaking up, but deep down they are still calculating chip allocations.
